AG.LND.FRLS.HA.name: Tree Cover Loss (hectares)
AG.LND.FRLS.HA.definition: Shows year-by-year tree cover loss, defined as stand level replacement of vegetation greater than 5 meters, within the selected area. The tree cover loss data set is a collaboration of the University of Maryland, Google, USGS, and NASA, and uses Landsat satellite images to map annual tree cover loss at a 30 × 30 meter resolution. Note that “tree cover loss” is not the same as “deforestation” – tree cover loss includes change in both natural and planted forest, and does not need to be human caused. The data from 2011 onward were produced with an updated methodology that may capture additional loss. Comparisons between the original 2001-2010 data and future years should be performed with caution.
AG.LND.FRLS.HA.organization: Global Forest Watch. Tree Cover Loss (Hansen/UMD/Google/USGS/NASA).

AG.LND.FRST.K2.name: Forest area (sq. km)
AG.LND.FRST.K2.definition: Forest area is land under natural or planted stands of trees of at least 5 meters in situ, whether productive or not, and excludes tree stands in agricultural production systems (for example, in fruit plantations and agroforestry systems) and trees in urban parks and gardens.
AG.LND.FRST.K2.organization: FAOSTAT, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), uri: https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/RL, publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

BG.GSR.NFSV.GD.ZS.name: Trade in services (% of GDP)
BG.GSR.NFSV.GD.ZS.definition: Total trade in services includes services provided by residents to non-residents plus services provided by non-residents to residents. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

birth_reg.name: Children under age 5 whose births are registered, total (%)
birth_reg.definition: Percentage of children under age 5 who were registered at the moment of the survey. The numerator of this indicator includes children reported to have a birth certificate, regardless of whether or not it was seen by the interviewer, and those without a birth certificate whose mother or caregiver says the birth has been registered, total.

birth_reg_1.name: Children under age 5 whose births are registered, female (%)
birth_reg_1.definition: Percentage of children under age 5 who were registered at the moment of the survey. The numerator of this indicator includes children reported to have a birth certificate, regardless of whether or not it was seen by the interviewer, and those without a birth certificate whose mother or caregiver says the birth has been registered, women.

birth_reg_2.name: Children under age 5 whose births are registered, male (%)
birth_reg_2.definition: Percentage of children under age 5 who were registered at the moment of the survey. The numerator of this indicator includes children reported to have a birth certificate, regardless of whether or not it was seen by the interviewer, and those without a birth certificate whose mother or caregiver says the birth has been registered, men.

BM.GSR.CMCP.ZS.name: Communications, computer, etc. (% of service imports, BoP)
BM.GSR.CMCP.ZS.definition: Communications, computer, information, and other services cover international telecommunications; computer data; news-related service transactions between residents and nonresidents; construction services; royalties and license fees; miscellaneous business, professional, and technical services; personal, cultural, and recreational services; manufacturing services on physical inputs owned by others; and maintenance and repair services and government services not included elsewhere. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of service imports which are services provided by non-residents to residents.
BM.GSR.CMCP.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.FCTY.CD.name: Primary income payments (BoP, current US$)
BM.GSR.FCTY.CD.definition: Primary income payments refer to employee compensation paid to nonresident workers and investment income (payments on direct investment, portfolio investment, other investments).This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BM.GSR.FCTY.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.GNFS.CD.name: Imports of goods and services (BoP, current US$)
BM.GSR.GNFS.CD.definition:
Imports of goods includes change in the economic ownership of goods from non-residents to




residents of the compiling economy, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. Imports of services includes services provided by non-residents to residents. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BM.GSR.GNFS.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.INSF.ZS.name: Insurance and financial services (% of service imports, BoP)
BM.GSR.INSF.ZS.definition: Insurance and financial services cover various types of insurance provided to nonresidents by resident insurance enterprises and vice versa, and financial intermediary and auxiliary services (except those of insurance enterprises and pension funds) exchanged between residents and nonresidents. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of service imports which are services provided by non-residents to residents.
BM.GSR.INSF.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.MRCH.CD.name: Goods imports (BoP, current US$)
BM.GSR.MRCH.CD.definition: Imports of goods occur when there are changes in the economic ownership of goods from non-residents to residents of the compiling economy, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BM.GSR.MRCH.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.NFSV.CD.name: Service imports (BoP, current US$)
BM.GSR.NFSV.CD.definition: Imports of services are services provided by non-residents to residents. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BM.GSR.NFSV.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.ROYL.CD.name: Charges for the use of intellectual property, payments (BoP, current US$)
BM.GSR.ROYL.CD.definition: Charges for the use of proprietary rights (such as patents, trademarks, copyrights, industrial processes and designs including trade secrets, franchises), and charges for licenses to reproduce or distribute (or both) intellectual property embodied in produced originals or prototypes (such as copyrights on books and manuscripts, computer software, cinematographic works, and sound recordings) and related rights (such as for live performances and television, cable, or satellite broadcast). This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BM.GSR.ROYL.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.TOTL.CD.name: Imports of goods, services and primary income (BoP, current US$)
BM.GSR.TOTL.CD.definition:
Imports of goods includes change in the economic ownership of goods from non-residents to




residents of the compiling economy, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. Imports of services includes services provided by non-residents to residents. Primary income represents the return that accrues to institutional units for their contribution to the production process or for the provision of financial assets and renting natural resources to other institutional units. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BM.GSR.TOTL.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.TRAN.ZS.name: Transport services (% of service imports, BoP)
BM.GSR.TRAN.ZS.definition: Transport services covers the process of carriage of people and objects from one location to another as well as related supporting and auxiliary services. Also included are postal and courier services. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of service imports which are services provided by non-residents to residents.
BM.GSR.TRAN.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.GSR.TRVL.ZS.name: Travel services (% of service imports, BoP)
BM.GSR.TRVL.ZS.definition: Travel services cover goods and services for own use or to give away acquired from an economy by nonresidents during visits to that economy, or acquired from other economies by residents during visits to these other economies. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of service imports which are services provided by non-residents to residents.
BM.GSR.TRVL.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.KLT.DINV.CD.WD.name: Foreign direct investment, net outflows (BoP, current US$)
BM.KLT.DINV.CD.WD.definition: Foreign direct investment refers to direct investment equity flows in an economy. It is the sum of equity capital, reinvestment of earnings, and other capital. Direct investment is a category of cross-border investment associated with a resident in one economy having control or a significant degree of influence on the management of an enterprise that is resident in another economy. Ownership of 10 percent or more of the ordinary shares of voting stock is the criterion for determining the existence of a direct investment relationship. This series shows net outflows of investment from the reporting economy to the rest of the world. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

BM.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS.name: Foreign direct investment, net outflows (% of GDP)
BM.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS.definition: Foreign direct investment refers to direct investment equity flows in an economy. It is the sum of equity capital, reinvestment of earnings, and other capital. Direct investment is a category of cross-border investment associated with a resident in one economy having control or a significant degree of influence on the management of an enterprise that is resident in another economy. Ownership of 10 percent or more of the ordinary shares of voting stock is the criterion for determining the existence of a direct investment relationship. This series shows net outflows of investment from the reporting economy to the rest of the world, and is divided by GDP.

BM.TRF.PRVT.CD.name: Secondary income, other sectors, payments (BoP, current US$)
BM.TRF.PRVT.CD.definition: Secondary income refers to transfers recorded in the balance of payments whenever an economy provides or receives goods, services, income, or financial items without a quid pro quo. All transfers not considered to be capital are current. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BM.TRF.PRVT.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BM.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.name: Personal remittances, paid (current US$)
BM.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.definition: Personal remittances comprise personal transfers and compensation of employees. Personal transfers consist of all current transfers in cash or in kind made or received by resident households to or from nonresident households. Personal transfers thus include all current transfers between resident and nonresident individuals. Compensation of employees refers to the income of border, seasonal, and other short-term workers who are employed in an economy where they are not resident and of residents employed by nonresident entities. Data are the sum of two items defined in the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual: personal transfers and compensation of employees. Data are in current U.S. dollars.
BM.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.organization:
IMF balance of payments data, International Monetary Fund (IMF);
Staff estimates, World Bank (WB)

BN.CAB.XOKA.CD.name: Current account balance (BoP, current US$)
BN.CAB.XOKA.CD.definition: Balance of current transactions (transactions in goods and services, earned income and transfer income) between residents and non-residents. The term current account balance is used in the external accounts and is expressed from the perspective of resident units. The term current external balance is used in the national accounts and is expressed from the perspective of the non-resident units, and therefore with the opposite sign. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.CAB.XOKA.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS.name: Current account balance (% of GDP)
BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS.definition: Balance of current transactions (transactions in goods and services, earned income and transfer income) between residents and non-residents. The term current account balance is used in the external accounts and is expressed from the perspective of resident units. The term current external balance is used in the national accounts and is expressed from the perspective of the non-resident units, and therefore with the opposite sign. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

BN.FIN.TOTL.CD.name: Net financial account (BoP, current US$)
BN.FIN.TOTL.CD.definition: The net financial account shows net acquisition and disposal of financial assets and liabilities. It measures how net lending to or borrowing from nonresidents is financed, and is conceptually equal to the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.FIN.TOTL.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.GSR.FCTY.CD.name: Net primary income (BoP, current US$)
BN.GSR.FCTY.CD.definition: Net primary income includes the net labor income and net property and entrepreneurial income components of the SNA. Labor income covers compensation of employees paid to nonresident workers. Property and entrepreneurial income covers investment income from the ownership of foreign financial claims (interest, dividends, rent, etc.) and nonfinancial property income (patents, copyrights, etc.). This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.GSR.FCTY.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.GSR.GNFS.CD.name: Net trade in goods and services (BoP, current US$)
BN.GSR.GNFS.CD.definition: The balance of international trade in goods and services is the difference between the exports and imports of goods and services. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.GSR.GNFS.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.GSR.MRCH.CD.name: Net trade in goods (BoP, current US$)
BN.GSR.MRCH.CD.definition: The balance of international trade in goods is the difference between the exports and imports of goods. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.GSR.MRCH.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.KAC.EOMS.CD.name: Net errors and omissions (BoP, current US$)
BN.KAC.EOMS.CD.definition: Net errors and omissions constitute a residual category needed to ensure that accounts in the balance of payments statement sum to zero. Net errors and omissions are derived as the balance on the financial account minus the balances on the current and capital accounts. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.KAC.EOMS.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.KLT.DINV.CD.name: Foreign direct investment, net (BoP, current US$)
BN.KLT.DINV.CD.definition: Foreign direct investment is a category of cross-border investment associated with a resident in one economy having control or a significant degree of influence on the management of an enterprise that is resident in another economy. Ownership of 10 percent or more of the voting power is evidence of a direct investment relationship. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.KLT.DINV.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.KLT.PTXL.CD.name: Portfolio Investment, net (BoP, current US$)
BN.KLT.PTXL.CD.definition: Portfolio investment includes cross-border flows and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.KLT.PTXL.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.RES.INCL.CD.name: Reserves and related items (BoP, current US$)
BN.RES.INCL.CD.definition: Reserves and related items is the net change in a country's holdings of international reserves resulting from transactions on the current, capital, and financial accounts. Reserve assets are external assets, including monetary gold, that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency.Also included are net credit and loans from the IMF (excluding reserve position) and total exceptional financing. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.RES.INCL.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.TRF.CURR.CD.name: Net secondary income (BoP, current US$)
BN.TRF.CURR.CD.definition: Net secondary income (from abroad) comprises transfers of income between residents of the reporting country and the rest of the world that carry no provisions for repayment. Net secondary income is equal to the unrequited transfers of income from nonresidents to residents minus the unrequited transfers from residents to nonresidents. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.TRF.CURR.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BN.TRF.KOGT.CD.name: Net capital account (BoP, current US$)
BN.TRF.KOGT.CD.definition: Net capital account records acquisitions and disposals of nonproduced nonfinancial assets, such as land sold to embassies and sales of leases and licenses, as well as capital transfers, including government debt forgiveness. The use of the term capital account in this context is designed to be consistent with the System of National Accounts, which distinguishes between capital transactions and financial transactions. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BN.TRF.KOGT.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.CCIS.CD.name: ICT service exports (BoP, current US$)
BX.GSR.CCIS.CD.definition: Information and communication technology service exports include computer and communications services (telecommunications and postal and courier services) and information services (computer data and news-related service transactions). Data are in current U.S. dollars.
BX.GSR.CCIS.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS.name: ICT service exports (% of service exports, BoP)
BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS.definition: Information and communication technology service exports include computer and communications services (telecommunications and postal and courier services) and information services (computer data and news-related service transactions).
BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.CMCP.ZS.name: Communications, computer, etc. (% of service exports, BoP)
BX.GSR.CMCP.ZS.definition: Communications, computer, information, and other services cover international telecommunications; computer data; news-related service transactions between residents and nonresidents; construction services; royalties and license fees; miscellaneous business, professional, and technical services; personal, cultural, and recreational services; manufacturing services on physical inputs owned by others; and maintenance and repair services and government services not included elsewhere. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of service exports which are services provided by residents to non-residents.
BX.GSR.CMCP.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.FCTY.CD.name: Primary income receipts (BoP, current US$)
BX.GSR.FCTY.CD.definition: Primary income receipts refer to employee compensation paid to resident workers working abroad and investment income (receipts on direct investment, portfolio investment, other investments, and receipts on reserve assets). This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BX.GSR.FCTY.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.GNFS.CD.name: Exports of goods and services (BoP, current US$)
BX.GSR.GNFS.CD.definition: Exports of goods includes changes in the economic ownership of goods from residents of the compiling economy to non-residents, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. Exports of services includes services provided by residents to non-residents. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BX.GSR.GNFS.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.INSF.ZS.name: Insurance and financial services (% of service exports, BoP)
BX.GSR.INSF.ZS.definition: Insurance and financial services cover various types of insurance provided to nonresidents by resident insurance enterprises and vice versa, and financial intermediary and auxiliary services (except those of insurance enterprises and pension funds) exchanged between residents and nonresidents. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of service exports which are services provided by residents to non-residents.
BX.GSR.INSF.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.MRCH.CD.name: Goods exports (BoP, current US$)
BX.GSR.MRCH.CD.definition: Exports of goods occur when there are changes in the economic ownership of goods from residents of the compiling economy to non-residents, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BX.GSR.MRCH.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.NFSV.CD.name: Service exports (BoP, current US$)
BX.GSR.NFSV.CD.definition: Exports of services are services provided by residents to non-residents. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BX.GSR.NFSV.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.ROYL.CD.name: Charges for the use of intellectual property, receipts (BoP, current US$)
BX.GSR.ROYL.CD.definition: Charges for the use of proprietary rights (such as patents, trademarks, copyrights, industrial processes and designs including trade secrets, franchises), and charges for licenses to reproduce or distribute (or both) intellectual property embodied in produced originals or prototypes (such as copyrights on books and manuscripts, computer software, cinematographic works, and sound recordings) and related rights (such as for live performances and television, cable, or satellite broadcast). This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BX.GSR.ROYL.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.TOTL.CD.name: Exports of goods, services and primary income (BoP, current US$)
BX.GSR.TOTL.CD.definition: Exports of goods includes changes in the economic ownership of goods from residents of the compiling economy to non-residents, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. Exports of services includes services provided by residents to non-residents. Primary income represents the return that accrues to institutional units for their contribution to the production process or for the provision of financial assets and renting natural resources to other institutional units. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BX.GSR.TOTL.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.TRAN.ZS.name: Transport services (% of service exports, BoP)
BX.GSR.TRAN.ZS.definition: Transport services covers the process of carriage of people and objects from one location to another as well as related supporting and auxiliary services. Also included are postal and courier services. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of service exports which are services provided by residents to non-residents.
BX.GSR.TRAN.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.GSR.TRVL.ZS.name: Travel services (% of service exports, BoP)
BX.GSR.TRVL.ZS.definition: Travel services cover goods and services for own use or to give away acquired from an economy by nonresidents during visits to that economy, or acquired from other economies by residents during visits to these other economies. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of service exports which are services provided by residents to non-residents.
BX.GSR.TRVL.ZS.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.KLT.DINV.CD.WD.name: Foreign direct investment, net inflows (BoP, current US$)
BX.KLT.DINV.CD.WD.definition: Foreign direct investment refers to direct investment equity flows in the reporting economy. It is the sum of equity capital, reinvestment of earnings, and other capital. Direct investment is a category of cross-border investment associated with a resident in one economy having control or a significant degree of influence on the management of an enterprise that is resident in another economy. Ownership of 10 percent or more of the ordinary shares of voting stock is the criterion for determining the existence of a direct investment relationship. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS.name: Foreign direct investment, net inflows (% of GDP)
BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS.definition: Foreign direct investment is the net inflows of investment to acquire a lasting management interest (10 percent or more of voting stock) in an enterprise operating in an economy other than that of the investor. It is the sum of equity capital, reinvestment of earnings, other long-term capital, and short-term capital as shown in the balance of payments. This series shows net inflows (new investment inflows less disinvestment) in the reporting economy from foreign investors, and is divided by GDP.

BX.PEF.TOTL.CD.WD.name: Portfolio equity, net inflows (BoP, current US$)
BX.PEF.TOTL.CD.WD.definition: Portfolio equity includes net inflows from equity securities other than those recorded as direct investment and including shares, stocks, depository receipts (American or global), and direct purchases of shares in local stock markets by foreign investors. Data are in current U.S. dollars.
BX.PEF.TOTL.CD.WD.organization:
Balance of Payments database, International Monetary Fund (IMF);
International Debt Statistics, World Bank (WB)

BX.TRF.CURR.CD.name: Secondary income receipts (BoP, current US$)
BX.TRF.CURR.CD.definition: Secondary income refers to transfers recorded in the balance of payments whenever an economy provides or receives goods, services, income, or financial items without a quid pro quo. All transfers not considered to be capital are current. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BX.TRF.CURR.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.name: Personal transfers, receipts (BoP, current US$)
BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.definition: Personal transfers are current transfers, in cash or in kind, received by resident households from non-resident households. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.organization: Balance of Payments Statistics Yearbook and data files, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.name: Personal remittances, received (current US$)
BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.definition: Personal remittances comprise personal transfers and compensation of employees. Personal transfers consist of all current transfers in cash or in kind made or received by resident households to or from nonresident households. Personal transfers thus include all current transfers between resident and nonresident individuals. Compensation of employees refers to the income of border, seasonal, and other short-term workers who are employed in an economy where they are not resident and of residents employed by nonresident entities. Data are the sum of two items defined in the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual: personal transfers and compensation of employees. Data are in current U.S. dollars.
BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.organization:
IMF balance of payments data, International Monetary Fund (IMF);
Staff estimates, World Bank (WB)

BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS.name: Personal remittances, received (% of GDP)
BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS.definition: Personal remittances comprise personal transfers and compensation of employees. Personal transfers consist of all current transfers in cash or in kind made or received by resident households to or from nonresident households. Personal transfers thus include all current transfers between resident and nonresident individuals. Compensation of employees refers to the income of border, seasonal, and other short-term workers who are employed in an economy where they are not resident and of residents employed by nonresident entities. Data are the sum of two items defined in the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual: personal transfers and compensation of employees.

CM.MKT.INDX.ZG.name: S&P Global Equity Indices (annual % change)
CM.MKT.INDX.ZG.definition: S&P Global Equity Indices measure the U.S. dollar price change in the stock markets covered by the S&P BMI country indices.
CM.MKT.INDX.ZG.organization: S&P Global BMI, S&P Dow Jones Indices, uri: https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/index-family/equity/global-equity/sp-global-bmi/#overview

CM.MKT.LCAP.CD.name: Market capitalization of listed domestic companies (current US$)
CM.MKT.LCAP.CD.definition: Market capitalization (also known as market value) is the share price times the number of shares outstanding (including their several classes) for listed domestic companies. Investment funds, unit trusts, and companies whose only business goal is to hold shares of other listed companies are excluded. Data are end of year values converted to U.S. dollars using corresponding year-end foreign exchange rates.
CM.MKT.LCAP.CD.organization: World Federation of Exchanges database, World Federation of Exchanges (WFE)

CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS.name: Market capitalization of listed domestic companies (% of GDP)
CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS.definition: Market capitalization (also known as market value) is the share price times the number of shares outstanding (including their several classes) for listed domestic companies. Investment funds, unit trusts, and companies whose only business goal is to hold shares of other listed companies are excluded. Data are end of year values.
CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS.organization: World Federation of Exchanges database, World Federation of Exchanges (WFE)

CM.MKT.LDOM.NO.name: Listed domestic companies, total
CM.MKT.LDOM.NO.definition: Listed domestic companies, including foreign companies which are exclusively listed, are those which have shares listed on an exchange at the end of the year. Investment funds, unit trusts, and companies whose only business goal is to hold shares of other listed companies, such as holding companies and investment companies, regardless of their legal status, are excluded. A company with several classes of shares is counted once. Only companies admitted to listing on the exchange are included.
CM.MKT.LDOM.NO.organization: World Federation of Exchanges database, World Federation of Exchanges (WFE)

CM.MKT.TRAD.CD.name: Stocks traded, total value (current US$)
CM.MKT.TRAD.CD.definition: The value of shares traded is the total number of shares traded, both domestic and foreign, multiplied by their respective matching prices. Figures are single counted (only one side of the transaction is considered). Companies admitted to listing and admitted to trading are included in the data. Data are end of year values converted to U.S. dollars using corresponding year-end foreign exchange rates.
CM.MKT.TRAD.CD.organization: World Federation of Exchanges database, World Federation of Exchanges (WFE)

CM.MKT.TRAD.GD.ZS.name: Stocks traded, total value (% of GDP)
CM.MKT.TRAD.GD.ZS.definition: The value of shares traded is the total number of shares traded, both domestic and foreign, multiplied by their respective matching prices. Figures are single counted (only one side of the transaction is considered). Companies admitted to listing and admitted to trading are included in the data. Data are end of year values.
CM.MKT.TRAD.GD.ZS.organization: World Federation of Exchanges database, World Federation of Exchanges (WFE)

diff_elections_s.name: Challenge: Participating in elections, total (% of population ages 15+ without an ID)
diff_elections_s.definition: The percentage of adult respondents without an ID who report that one limitation that they experience because they lack an ID is the inability to participate in elections. If the minimum age for obtaining an ID is above 15, observations below the minimum age are excluded, total sample.

diff_finance_s.name: Challenge: Using financial services, total (% of population ages 15+ without an ID)
diff_finance_s.definition: The percentage of adult respondents without an ID who report that one limitation that they experience because they lack an ID is the inability to open a bank account. If the minimum age for obtaining an ID is above 15, observations below the minimum age are excluded, total sample.

diff_gov_s.name: Challenge: Receiving financial support, total (% of population ages 15+ without an ID)
diff_gov_s.definition: The percentage of adult respondents without an ID who report that one limitation that they experience because they lack an ID is the inability to receive financial support from the government. If the minimum age for obtaining an ID is above 15, observations below the minimum age are excluded, total sample.

diff_job_s.name: Challenge: Applying for a job, total (% of population ages 15+ without an ID)
diff_job_s.definition: The percentage of adult respondents without an ID who report that one limitation that they experience because they lack an ID is the inability apply for a job. If the minimum age for obtaining an ID is above 15, observations below the minimum age are excluded, total sample.

diff_med_s.name: Challenge: Receiving medical care, total (% of population ages 15+ without an ID)
diff_med_s.definition: The percentage of adult respondents without an ID who report that one limitation that they experience because they lack an ID is the inability to use financial services. If the minimum age for obtaining an ID is above 15, observations below the minimum age are excluded, total sample.

diff_sim_s.name: Challenge: Obtaining a SIM card (% of population ages 15+ without an ID)
diff_sim_s.definition: The percentage of adult respondents without an ID who report that one limitation that they experience because they lack an ID is the inability to obtain a SIM card. If the minimum age for obtaining an ID is above 15, observations below the minimum age are excluded, total sample.

EF.EFM.UNIV.XD.name: Universal Economic Fitness Metric
EF.EFM.UNIV.XD.definition: The Universal Economic Fitness (UEF) is both a measure of a country’s diversification and ability to produce complex goods on a globally competitive basis.  Countries with the highest levels of EF have capabilities to produce a diverse portfolio of products, ability to upgrade into ever-increasing complex goods, tend to have more predictable long-term growth, and to attain good competitive position relative to other countries.   Countries with low UEF levels tend to suffer from poverty, low capabilities, less predictable growth, low value-addition, and trouble upgrading and diversifying faster than other countries.  The starting data is the COMTRADE list of products and the IMF-BOP list of services exported by each country. This data defines a bipartite network of countries and sectors, or goods and services. A suitably designed mathematical algorithm applied to this network leads to the Universal Economic Fitness of all countries and the Complexity of all sectors. The comparison of the Fitness to the GDP reveals hidden information for the development and the growth of the countries.
EF.EFM.UNIV.XD.organization: World Bank, Economic Fitness project. For more details please visit the following links. The Fitness and Complexity algorithm has been introduced in: https://www.nature.com/articles/srep00723 For a detailed discussion of the data preprocessing, the computation of the universal fitness, and the economical implications: http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/309521529586431853/Integrating-services-in-the-economic-fitness-approach The convergence criterion of the Fitness and Complexity algorithm is discussed in: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1140/epjst/e2015-50118-1

EG.ELC.COAL.ZS.name: Electricity production from coal sources (% of total)
EG.ELC.COAL.ZS.definition: The share of electricity production from coal sources of total electricity production. Sources of electricity refer to the inputs used to generate electricity. Coal refers to all coal and brown coal, both primary (including hard coal and lignite-brown coal) and derived fuels (including patent fuel, coke oven coke, gas coke, coke oven gas, and blast furnace gas). Peat is also included in this category.
EG.ELC.COAL.ZS.organization: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25

EG.ELC.FOSL.ZS.name: Electricity production from oil, gas and coal sources (% of total)
EG.ELC.FOSL.ZS.definition: The share of electricity production from oil, gas and coal sources of total electricity production. Sources of electricity refer to the inputs used to generate electricity. Oil refers to crude oil and petroleum products. Gas refers to natural gas but excludes natural gas liquids. Coal refers to all coal and brown coal, both primary (including hard coal and lignite-brown coal) and derived fuels (including patent fuel, coke oven coke, gas coke, coke oven gas, and blast furnace gas). Peat is also included in this category.
EG.ELC.FOSL.ZS.organization: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25

EG.ELC.HYRO.ZS.name: Electricity production from hydroelectric sources (% of total)
EG.ELC.HYRO.ZS.definition: The share of electricity production from hydroelectric sources of total electricity production. Sources of electricity refer to the inputs used to generate electricity. Hydropower refers to electricity produced by hydroelectric power plants.
EG.ELC.HYRO.ZS.organization: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25

EG.ELC.LOSS.ZS.name: Electric power transmission and distribution losses (% of output)
EG.ELC.LOSS.ZS.definition: Electric power transmission and distribution losses include losses in transmission between sources of supply and points of distribution and in the distribution to consumers, including pilferage. The losses are expressed as a share of the total output.
EG.ELC.LOSS.ZS.organization: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25

EG.ELC.NGAS.ZS.name: Electricity production from natural gas sources (% of total)
EG.ELC.NGAS.ZS.definition: The share of electricity production from natural gas sources of total electricity production. Sources of electricity refer to the inputs used to generate electricity. Gas refers to natural gas but excludes natural gas liquids.
EG.ELC.NGAS.ZS.organization: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25

EG.ELC.NUCL.ZS.name: Electricity production from nuclear sources (% of total)
EG.ELC.NUCL.ZS.definition: The share of electricity production from nuclear sources of total electricity production. Sources of electricity refer to the inputs used to generate electricity. Nuclear power refers to electricity produced by nuclear power plants.
EG.ELC.NUCL.ZS.organization: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25

EG.ELC.PETR.ZS.name: Electricity production from oil sources (% of total)
EG.ELC.PETR.ZS.definition: The share of electricity production from oil sources of total electricity production. Sources of electricity refer to the inputs used to generate electricity. Oil refers to crude oil and petroleum products.
EG.ELC.PETR.ZS.organization: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25

EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.name: Electric power consumption (kWh per capita)
EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.definition: Electric power consumption measures the production of power plants and combined heat and power plants less transmission, distribution, and transformation losses and own use by heat and power plants.
EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.organization: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25

EN.URB.LCTY.name: Population in largest city
EN.URB.LCTY.definition: Population in largest city is the urban population living in the country's largest metropolitan area.
EN.URB.LCTY.organization: World Urbanization Prospects 2018, United Nations (UN), uri: https://population.un.org/wup/, publisher: UN Population Division, date published: 2018

EN.URB.LCTY.UR.ZS.name: Population in the largest city (% of urban population)
EN.URB.LCTY.UR.ZS.definition: Population in largest city is the percentage of a country's urban population living in that country's largest metropolitan area.
EN.URB.LCTY.UR.ZS.organization: World Urbanization Prospects 2018, United Nations (UN), uri: https://population.un.org/wup/, publisher: UN Population Division, date published: 2018

EN.URB.MCTY.name: Population in urban agglomerations of more than 1 million
EN.URB.MCTY.definition: Population in urban agglomerations of more than one million is the country's population living in metropolitan areas that in 2018 had a population of more than one million people.
EN.URB.MCTY.organization: World Urbanization Prospects 2018, United Nations (UN), uri: https://population.un.org/wup/, publisher: UN Population Division, date published: 2018

EN.URB.MCTY.TL.ZS.name: Population in urban agglomerations of more than 1 million (% of total population)
EN.URB.MCTY.TL.ZS.definition: Population in urban agglomerations of more than one million is the percentage of a country's population living in metropolitan areas that in 2018 had a population of more than one million people.
EN.URB.MCTY.TL.ZS.organization: World Urbanization Prospects 2018, United Nations (UN), uri: https://population.un.org/wup/, publisher: UN Population Division, date published: 2018

ER.LND.PTLD.ZS.name: Terrestrial protected areas (% of total land area)
ER.LND.PTLD.ZS.definition: Terrestrial protected areas are totally or partially protected areas of at least 1,000 hectares that are designated by national authorities as scientific reserves with limited public access, national parks, natural monuments, nature reserves or wildlife sanctuaries, protected landscapes, and areas managed mainly for sustainable use. Marine areas, unclassified areas, littoral (intertidal) areas, and sites protected under local or provincial law are excluded.
ER.LND.PTLD.ZS.organization:
Protected Planet: The World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) and World Database on Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (WD-OECM), UN Environment Programme World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC), uri: https://www.protectedplanet.net/en, publisher: Protected Planet, date accessed: 20240516, date published: 202405;
International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), uri: https://www.protectedplanet.net/en, publisher: Protected Planet, date accessed: 20240516

ER.MRN.PTMR.ZS.name: Marine protected areas (% of territorial waters)
ER.MRN.PTMR.ZS.definition: Marine protected areas are areas of intertidal or subtidal terrain--and overlying water and associated flora and fauna and historical and cultural features--that have been reserved by law or other effective means to protect part or all of the enclosed environment.
ER.MRN.PTMR.ZS.organization:
Protected Planet: The World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) and World Database on Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (WD-OECM), UN Environment Programme World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC), uri: https://www.protectedplanet.net/en, note: Only the latest data can be retrieved from the Protected Planet website. The time series are provided directly to WDI by Protected Planet., publisher: Protected Planet, date accessed: 20240516, date published: 202405;
International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), uri: https://www.protectedplanet.net/en, publisher: Protected Planet, date accessed: 20240516

ER.PTD.TOTL.ZS.name: Terrestrial and marine protected areas (% of total territorial area)
ER.PTD.TOTL.ZS.definition: Terrestrial protected areas are totally or partially protected areas of at least 1,000 hectares that are designated by national authorities as scientific reserves with limited public access, national parks, natural monuments, nature reserves or wildlife sanctuaries, protected landscapes, and areas managed mainly for sustainable use. Marine protected areas are areas of intertidal or subtidal terrain--and overlying water and associated flora and fauna and historical and cultural features--that have been reserved by law or other effective means to protect part or all of the enclosed environment. Sites protected under local or provincial law are excluded.
ER.PTD.TOTL.ZS.organization:
Protected Planet: The World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) and World Database on Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (WD-OECM), UN Environment Programme World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC), uri: https://www.protectedplanet.net/en, publisher: Protected Planet, date accessed: 20240516, date published: 202405;
International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), uri: https://www.protectedplanet.net/en, publisher: Protected Planet, date accessed: 20240516

FB.AST.NPER.ZS.name: Bank nonperforming loans to total gross loans (%)
FB.AST.NPER.ZS.definition: The indicator measures the proportion of a deposit taker’s loan portfolio that is impaired or at risk of default. It is calculated as the ratio of non-performing loans (NPLs) to total gross loans, where NPLs are defined as loans that are past due by 90 days or more or are otherwise considered unlikely to be repaid in full without the realization of collateral. Both non-performing loans and total gross loans should be reported at their gross book value, without deducting for loan-loss provisions or collateral. This indicator provides a key measure of asset quality and potential credit risk in the banking system.
FB.AST.NPER.ZS.organization: Financial Soundness Indicators, International Monetary Fund (IMF), uri: https://data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF:EXTERNAL_DATASET_CARDS/IMF.STA:LFSI

FB.BNK.CAPA.ZS.name: Bank capital to assets ratio (%)
FB.BNK.CAPA.ZS.definition: The indicator is a measure of capital adequacy that evaluates the financial strength of deposit takers by comparing Tier 1 capital to total assets. Tier 1 capital, often referred to as core capital, includes the most stable and readily available forms of capital, such as common equity, disclosed reserves, retained earnings, and certain other instruments that meet regulatory requirements under the Basel framework. This capital is considered the highest quality because it is fully available to cover losses and does not need to be repaid.

FD.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.name: Domestic credit to private sector by banks (% of GDP)
FD.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.definition: Domestic credit to private sector by banks refers to financial resources provided to the private sector by other depository corporations (deposit taking corporations except central banks), such as through loans, purchases of nonequity securities, and trade credits and other accounts receivable, that establish a claim for repayment. For some countries these claims include credit to public enterprises. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

FD.RES.LIQU.AS.ZS.name: Bank liquid reserves to bank assets ratio (%)
FD.RES.LIQU.AS.ZS.definition: Ratio of bank liquid reserves to bank assets is the ratio of domestic currency holdings and deposits with the monetary authorities to claims on other governments, nonfinancial public enterprises, the private sector, and other banking institutions. This indicator is expressed as a percentage (a÷b)*100.
FD.RES.LIQU.AS.ZS.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FI.RES.TOTL.CD.name: Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)
FI.RES.TOTL.CD.definition: Reserve assets are external assets, including monetary gold, that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
FI.RES.TOTL.CD.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FI.RES.TOTL.MO.name: Total reserves in months of imports
FI.RES.TOTL.MO.definition: Reserve assets are external assets, including monetary gold, that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. This item is expressed in terms of the number of months of imports of goods and services they could pay for [X/(Imports/12)].
FI.RES.TOTL.MO.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FI.RES.XGLD.CD.name: Total reserves minus gold (current US$)
FI.RES.XGLD.CD.definition: This series includes external assets (excluding monetary gold) that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.
FI.RES.XGLD.CD.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FM.AST.CGOV.ZG.M3.name: Claims on central government (annual growth as % of broad money)
FM.AST.CGOV.ZG.M3.definition: Claims on central government include loans to central government institutions net of deposits. Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value. This indicator represents the annual percentage growth in the ratio of claims to broad money.
FM.AST.CGOV.ZG.M3.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FM.AST.DOMO.ZG.M3.name: Claims on other sectors of the domestic economy (annual growth as % of broad money)
FM.AST.DOMO.ZG.M3.definition: Claims on other sectors of the domestic economy include gross credit from the financial system to households, nonprofit institutions serving households, nonfinancial corporations, state and local governments, and social security funds. Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value. This indicator represents the annual percentage growth in the ratio of claims to broad money.
FM.AST.DOMO.ZG.M3.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FM.AST.DOMS.CN.name: Net domestic credit (current LCU)
FM.AST.DOMS.CN.definition: Net domestic credit is the sum of net claims on the central government and claims on other sectors of the domestic economy. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This series is expressed in local currency units.
FM.AST.DOMS.CN.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FM.AST.NFRG.CN.name: Net foreign assets (current LCU)
FM.AST.NFRG.CN.definition: Net foreign assets are the sum of foreign assets held by monetary authorities and deposit money banks, less their foreign liabilities. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This series is expressed in local currency units.
FM.AST.NFRG.CN.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FM.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.name: Monetary Sector credit to private sector (% GDP)
FM.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.definition: Domestic credit to private sector refers to financial resources provided to the private sector, such as through loans, purchases of nonequity securities, and trade credits and other accounts receivable, that establish a claim for repayment. For some countries these claims include credit to public enterprises. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

FM.AST.PRVT.ZG.M3.name: Claims on private sector (annual growth as % of broad money)
FM.AST.PRVT.ZG.M3.definition: Claims on private sector include gross credit from the financial system to individuals, enterprises, nonfinancial public entities not included under net domestic credit, and financial institutions not included elsewhere. Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value. This indicator represents the annual percentage growth in the ratio of claims to broad money.
FM.AST.PRVT.ZG.M3.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FM.LBL.BMNY.CN.name: Broad money (current LCU)
FM.LBL.BMNY.CN.definition: Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This series is expressed in local currency units.
FM.LBL.BMNY.CN.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FM.LBL.BMNY.GD.ZS.name: Broad money (% of GDP)
FM.LBL.BMNY.GD.ZS.definition: Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

FM.LBL.BMNY.IR.ZS.name: Broad money to total reserves ratio
FM.LBL.BMNY.IR.ZS.definition: Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value.  Reserve assets are external assets, including monetary gold, that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. This indicator is expressed as a ratio (a÷b).
FM.LBL.BMNY.IR.ZS.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FM.LBL.BMNY.ZG.name: Broad money growth (annual %)
FM.LBL.BMNY.ZG.definition: Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value. This indicator denotes the percentage change over each previous year of the constant price (base year 2015) series in United States dollars.
FM.LBL.BMNY.ZG.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FP.CPI.TOTL.name: Consumer price index (2010 = 100)
FP.CPI.TOTL.definition: Index of the prices of consumption goods and services, as compared to a certain reference period (2010=100).
FP.CPI.TOTL.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.name: Inflation, consumer prices (annual %)
FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.definition: Inflation as measured by the consumer price index reflects the annual percentage change in the cost to the average consumer of acquiring a basket of goods and services that may be fixed or changed at specified intervals, such as yearly.
FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FR.INR.DPST.name: Deposit interest rate (%)
FR.INR.DPST.definition: Deposit interest rate is the rate paid by commercial or similar banks for demand, time, or savings deposits. The terms and conditions attached to these rates differ by country, however, limiting their comparability. This indicator is expressed as a percentage (a÷b)*100.
FR.INR.DPST.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FR.INR.LEND.name: Lending interest rate (%)
FR.INR.LEND.definition: Lending rate is the bank rate that usually meets the short- and medium-term financing needs of the private sector. This rate is normally differentiated according to creditworthiness of borrowers and objectives of financing. The terms and conditions attached to these rates differ by country, however, limiting their comparability.
FR.INR.LEND.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FR.INR.LNDP.name: Interest rate spread (lending rate minus deposit rate, %)
FR.INR.LNDP.definition: Interest rate spread is the interest rate charged by banks on loans to private sector customers minus the interest rate paid by commercial or similar banks for demand, time, or savings deposits. The terms and conditions attached to these rates differ by country, however, limiting their comparability.
FR.INR.LNDP.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FR.INR.RINR.name: Real interest rate (%)
FR.INR.RINR.definition: An interest rate is the amount charged, expressed as a percentage of the principal over a period of time, by the owners of certain kinds of financial assets for putting the financial assets at the disposal of another institutional unit. The real interest rate is the lending interest rate adjusted for inflation as measured by the GDP deflator. The terms and conditions attached to lending rates differ by country, however, limiting their comparability. This indicator is expressed as a percentage (a÷b)*100.
FR.INR.RINR.organization:
International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF);
World Development Indicators, World Bank (WB)

FR.INR.RISK.name: Risk premium on lending (lending rate minus treasury bill rate, %)
FR.INR.RISK.definition: Risk premium on lending is the interest rate charged by banks on loans to private sector customers minus the "risk free" treasury bill interest rate at which short-term government securities are issued or traded in the market. In some countries this spread may be negative, indicating that the market considers its best corporate clients to be lower risk than the government. The terms and conditions attached to lending rates differ by country, however, limiting their comparability.
FR.INR.RISK.organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

FS.AST.CGOV.GD.ZS.name: Claims on central government, etc. (% GDP)
FS.AST.CGOV.GD.ZS.definition: Claims on central government include loans to central government institutions net of deposits. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

FS.AST.DOMO.GD.ZS.name: Claims on other sectors of the domestic economy (% of GDP)
FS.AST.DOMO.GD.ZS.definition: Claims on other sectors of the domestic economy include gross credit from the financial system to households, nonprofit institutions serving households, nonfinancial corporations, state and local governments, and social security funds. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

FS.AST.DOMS.GD.ZS.name: Domestic credit provided by financial sector (% of GDP)
FS.AST.DOMS.GD.ZS.definition: Domestic credit provided by the financial sector includes all credit to various sectors on a gross basis, with the exception of credit to the central government, which is net. The financial sector includes monetary authorities and deposit money banks, as well as other financial corporations where data are available (including corporations that do not accept transferable deposits but do incur such liabilities as time and savings deposits). Examples of other financial corporations are finance and leasing companies, money lenders, insurance corporations, pension funds, and foreign exchange companies. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

FS.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.name: Domestic credit to private sector (% of GDP)
FS.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.definition: Domestic credit to private sector refers to financial resources provided to the private sector by financial corporations, such as through loans, purchases of nonequity securities, and trade credits and other accounts receivable, that establish a claim for repayment. For some countries these claims include credit to public enterprises. The financial corporations include monetary authorities and deposit money banks, as well as other financial corporations where data are available (including corporations that do not accept transferable deposits but do incur such liabilities as time and savings deposits). Examples of other financial corporations are finance and leasing companies, money lenders, insurance corporations, pension funds, and foreign exchange companies. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

GD_WBL_AST_ENF_INHERCHLD_E.name: WBL: Enforcement Perceptions, Assets, Public authorities enforce existing legislation granting equal inheritance rights to sons and daughters
GD_WBL_AST_ENF_INHERCHLD_E.definition:
The indicator assesses expert perceptions of the extent to which public authorities enforce existing legislation granting equal inheritance rights to sons and daughters in practice.Experts rate enforcement on a five-point Likert scale (0–4), where 0 indicates no enforcement of protective or beneficial laws, no upholding of women’s rights, or full enforcement of restrictive laws, and 4 indicates full enforcement of protective or beneficial laws, the full upholding of women’s rights, or no enforcement of restrictive laws.

Enforcement perceptions indicator-level scores are calculated by taking the median value of individual expert responses on the five-point Likert scale (0–4) for each indicator at the economy level. For indicators that correspond to a partially scored legal frameworks indicator, a weighted approach is applied, as described in detail in the enforcement perceptions scoring sections in the relevant topic chapters.

For details, please refer to the WBL Methodology Handbook (link: https://wbl.worldbank.org/content/dam/sites/wbl/documents/2026/WBL-Methodology-Handbook-2026-FINAL.pdf).
GD_WBL_AST_ENF_INHERCHLD_E.organization: World Bank: Women, Business and the Law. https://wbl.worldbank.org/
